title: Russia wins first medals of Winter Paralympics in 12 years with Voronchikhina, Bugaev successes
content:
CORTINA D’AMPEZZO, ITALY — On the opening day of the alpine skiing programme, Russia won two bronze medals. It is the first time Russia has won Paralympics medals for 12 years, when Sochi hosted the 2014 Games.

Varvara Voronchikhina came third in the downhill women’s standing classification. The 23-year-old, who was born without part of her left hand, raced third in a field of 16 athletes. Her time of 1:24.47s temporarily put her in top spot, before France’s Aurelie Richard (1:23.71s) and Swedish athlete Ebba Aarsjoe (1:22.00s) went quicker to claim silver and gold.

“I’m very happy because it’s (the) first medal for me,” she said after the event. “It was a bronze, but I’m really happy. I hope I will be skiing better in (the) next races.”

Voronchikhina added that she was “really sad” to have missed the 2022 Games, when Russia were suspended by the IPC following the invasion of Ukraine.

“It’s been a long time without the flag. All my country and all my teammates, we (are) glad.”

In the men’s standing race, Aleksei Bugaev also made the podium. He went 20th in a 38-man field, and was consistent with his splits on a fast, slick course, coming through in 1:18.94s. That put him third, behind Robin Kuche of Switzerland (1:17.79s, gold) and France’s Arthur Bauchet (1:18.40s, silver).

Bugaev, who was born without fingers or a thumb on his right hand, was a flag bearer for Russia last night at the opening ceremony in Verona. Seven eastern European countries —  Czechia, Estonia, Finland, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland and Ukraine — boycotted the ceremony because of the inclusion of Russia and Belarus in the Games.

Voronchikhina and Bugaev are two of six Russian athletes competing at these Paralympics. They, along with four Belarus athletes, were given what the International Paralympic Committee (IPC) call “bipartite” entries, which is automatic qualification for top-level competitors who do not qualify by traditional methods (typically because of injury or pregnancy).

Russia and Belarus were suspended from the past two Winter Paralympics. The IPC member nations voted against allowing them into the 2022 Games in Beijing, and four years before, Russia were banned from the Pyeongchang Games because of state-sponsored doping. Their athletes competed in 2018 under neutral conditions — without their flag and national anthem.

Last September, IPC members voted to lift the suspension. There had been a partial lifting in 2024 for the summer Paralympics in Paris, where Russian and Belarusian athletes were permitted to compete under neutral terms, like in 2018.

After taking FIS (the International Ski and Snowboard federation) to the Court of Arbitration for Sport last December, Russia managed to secure spots for their athletes, because their previous bans meant they had not been able to qualify through typical methods.

As such, this is a Paralympics debut for 23-year-old Voronchikhina, whereas Bugaev, now 28, is at his third Games. The IPC made the case that they only gave these spots out because of athlete quality. These were bona-fide athletes who would contend for medals.

Voronchikhina won six medals, including two golds, at the 2021 World Championships in Lillehammer, Norway. Bugaev arrived in Italy with three Paralympic titles and seven medals, having won two golds at his home Games in 2014, when he was just a teenager.

Both Voronchikhina and Bugaev are scheduled to compete in the full alpine ski programme — combined, slalom, giant slalom and super-G are still to come.

Russia also have two snowboarders, Dmitrii Fadeev and Filipp Shebbo, with medal events for that starting on Sunda). There is also Russian representation in cross-country skiing, with Ivan Golubkov (sit skier) and Anastasiia Bagiian (visually impaired).

All four Belarusian athletes are competing in cross-country skiing: Valiantsina Biryla and Lidziya Loban in the sitting classification. Darya Fedzkovich and Raman Svirydzenka are standing skiers. The medal events start on Tuesday.
